messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problem of R-INLA on a Linux machine (Same code is able to run on a Windows machine)
parts:
Hi,

the message is that something, for the first linear predictor, is either
INF or NAN, which is essentially that something is drifting off. try to
make it a big more stable (adding like

control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = 0.001)

if you think you need a proper prior for the intercept to make this
run.

different OS's seems to treat big number differently and hence you can
make it run on Linux but not on Windows, or the other way around.

If it does not work out, I can have a look if you send me R-code and
data to rerun it here.

Best
H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problem of R-INLA on a Linux machine (Same code is able to run on a Windows machine)
parts:
Hi Dr. Rue,

Thank you very much for this suggestions, but the problem remains when I put in a proper prior for the intercept as you suggested and changing the prior value did not help. Could you have a look at my code and help me out here?

Here is my code. It uses a small data set from CRAN. Please let me know if you have any questions about it.

install.packages("BayesianAnimalTracker")
library(BayesianAnimalTracker)
library(INLA)

data(Trip1GPS)
data(Trip1DR)
Trip1GPSformat <- GPStable(Trip1GPS)
Trip1GPSinKM <- DegToKM(Trip1GPSformat)
ndl <- as.dataList(Trip1DR$Ydim/1000, Trip1GPSinKM$Northing, 
                   Ytime=strptime(Trip1GPS$DateTime, "%d-%b-%Y %H:%M:%S"), 
                   Xtime=strptime(Trip1DR$DateTime, "%d-%b-%Y %H:%M:%S"), 
                   s2G=0.0625, timeUnit=60, betaOrder=1)

T <- nrow(ndl$XMx)
K <- ndl$glist$K     
mknots = seq(ndl$XMx[1,2], ndl$XMx[T,2], length = 300)
mMesh <- inla.mesh.1d(mknots, interval =range(ndl$XMx[,2]), degree = 2, boundary = "dirichlet")

spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mMesh)
time.index<- inla.spde.make.index("time", n.spde = spde$n.spde)

intVec <- c(rep(1, T), rep(0, K))
timeXC <- c(ndl$XMx[,2], rep(NA, K))
timeYC <- c(rep(NA, T), ndl$glist$Gtime)

A = inla.spde.make.A(mMesh, loc = c(ndl$XMx[,2], ndl$glist$Gtime))
stack = inla.stack(data = list(y = c(ndl$XMx[,1], ndl$glist$Y)), A = list(A, 1, 1, 1),
effects = list(time.index, list(intVec=intVec), 
list(timeXC=timeXC), list(timeYC=timeYC)),
tag = "est")
data = inla.stack.data(stack)

f1 <- y~ -1 + intVec + f(time, model = spde) + f(timeXC, model="rw1") + 
f(timeYC, model="iid", hyper=list(theta=list(fixed=TRUE, initial=log(1/0.0625))))


result = inla(f1, family = "gaussian", data = data,
control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stack),compute = TRUE),
control.family = list(hyper=list(prec=list(fixed=TRUE, initial=Inf))), 
  control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = 0.1),
verbose=TRUE)
 

Once again, the same code works well on the Windows machine, but not on Linux. I need the Linux machine to run the model on a similar but much larger data set. 

Thank you very much for your help.
Cheers, 
Seagle
